messages.content:
You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
Based on the chest X-ray in Figure 1, which of the following best describes the findings and their correlation with the patient’s history of lymphoma?
A. Bilateral peripheral nodular infiltrates suggestive of viral pneumonia, unrelated to the patient’s lymphoma history.
B. Bilateral interstitial infiltration with central distribution, consistent with lymphomatous infiltration related to the patient’s history of MALT lymphoma.
C. Unilateral alveolar consolidation in the right lung, indicating bacterial pneumonia, unrelated to the patient’s lymphoma history.
D. Bilateral perihilar lymphadenopathy, indicative of sarcoidosis, unrelated to the patient’s lymphoma history.
E. Diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities, suggestive of pulmonary edema, unrelated to the patient’s lymphoma history.
F. Unilateral pleural effusion on the left side, consistent with pleuritis, unrelated to the patient’s lymphoma history.
